left.title: Aaron meets Moses; Israel believes
left.excerpt: Aaron meets Moses in the wilderness, Moses recounts the commission, and together they gather Israel’s elders.
left.observation: The fear Moses voiced earlier—“What if they don’t believe me?”—meets an immediate answer when the people believe and bow after hearing that Yahweh has seen their affliction.

right.title: First confrontation makes things worse
right.excerpt: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go worship; Pharaoh increases the labor instead.
right.observation: The first public confrontation does not look like deliverance. Israel’s officers blame Moses and Aaron, and Moses turns back to God asking why the mission has brought greater harm.

anchor.title: Aaron meets Moses; Israel believes

left.title: “I am not able to bear all this people alone”
left.excerpt: Complaint about hardship and food escalates until Moses tells God that the burden of the people is too heavy for him.
left.observation: Moses describes the people with parental imagery—asking whether he conceived or gave birth to them—and says he cannot carry them alone.

right.title: Moses asks that Israel not be left without a shepherd
right.phase: The land approaches, but Moses will not enter

right.observation: Joshua is selected, brought before Eleazar and the congregation, commissioned publicly, and given some of Moses’ authority.

right.title: Israel refuses; Moses intercedes again
right.excerpt: Israel responds to the spies by wanting to return to Egypt and threatening new leadership.
right.observation: Moses and Aaron fall facedown; Joshua and Caleb appeal to the people; glory appears; Moses again argues from what Egypt and the nations will hear about God.

left.title: Leadership becomes distributed
left.excerpt: Jethro watches Moses judge the people alone from morning to evening and tells him the arrangement is not good.
left.observation: Moses is told to remain before God and teach the people, while capable leaders handle smaller disputes. The burden is redistributed before Sinai’s covenant scene begins.

right.title: Seventy elders share the burden
right.excerpt: God tells Moses to gather seventy elders; Spirit rests on them and they prophesy.
right.observation: When Joshua wants Eldad and Medad stopped, Moses answers that he wishes all Yahweh’s people were prophets and that Yahweh would put his Spirit on them.

right.title: “Show me your glory”
right.excerpt: Moses asks who will go with him, ties God’s presence to Israel’s distinct identity, and then asks to see God’s glory.
right.observation: The request grows from guidance, to presence, to knowledge, to glory. The answer grants a protected encounter but also names a limit.

right.title: Moses appears with Elijah beside Jesus

right.observation: Moses is present, but the scene’s final command directs attention to Jesus. After the voice, the disciples see no one except Jesus alone.

left.title: Violence, intervention, and flight
left.excerpt: Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, kills the Egyptian, and soon discovers that the act is known.
left.observation: The grown Moses identifies the Hebrew workers as his brothers, acts violently against an Egyptian, is challenged by another Hebrew, and becomes a fugitive from Pharaoh.

right.title: Stephen retells Moses’ life
right.excerpt: Stephen’s speech retells Moses as beautiful to God, educated in Egypt, rejected when he first tries to intervene, called in the wilderness, and sent as ruler and deliverer.
right.observation: The speech emphasizes rejection repeatedly: “Who made you a ruler and a judge?” appears again when Stephen narrates Israel’s later resistance to Moses.

left.observation: Israel cries out, Moses tells them to stand still and see Yahweh’s salvation, then Moses is told to move the people forward and stretch out his hand over the sea.

right.title: Meribah: Moses crosses a boundary

right.observation: Water still comes, but Moses and Aaron are told they did not believe God so as to sanctify him before Israel, and they will not bring the assembly into the land.

left.title: Moses sees the land and dies

capsuleTopic.title: Moses
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Rescued child · exile · reluctant messenger · deliverer · mediator · wilderness leader · final teacher · remembered servant
capsuleTopic.orientation: Do not reduce Moses to lawgiver, miracle worker, national hero, reluctant leader, or wilderness failure. Follow the whole narrative and let rescue, identity, resistance, mediation, burden, intimacy, judgment, succession, and later memory accumulate around the same person.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow Moses through changing places, audiences, authority, pressure, access, failures, responsibilities, and memory. Let later Scripture reopen earlier scenes instead of deciding who Moses is from one episode.

payload.description: Trace how different audiences respond to Moses before and after circumstances change.
